The lattice parameter of GaN films grown by molecular-beam epitaxy on different substrates depends on the nature of the substrate, with a value of 0.319 nm for films on GaN, 0.3191 nm for those grown on silicon carbide, and 0.3193 nm on sapphire.

the lattice parameter of the epitaxial film is strongly dependent on the nature of substrate and that the incorporation of shallow donors into GaN is also strongly influenced by the nature of substrate.
the lattice mismatch between the film and the substrate has a strong influence on the structural and optical characteristics of the film.

the growth and characterisation of GaN by molecular beam epitaxial methods.
the effects of substrate type on epitaxial film quality.
the effects of lattice parameter mismatch and thermal expansion coefficient mismatch between the substrate and the GaN film.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the substrate is a very important parameter in the epitaxial growth of GaN.
the substrate is the most important parameter in determining the quality of the GaN film.
the properties of the epitaxial GaN film are strongly influenced by the type of substrate used for growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the growth of good quality GaN epitaxials films, the substrate should be as close as possible to the GaN lattice parameter and have a low thermal expansion coefficient.
the best quality GaN epitaxially grown by molecular beam epixtaxy has been obtained on the GaN substrate.
GaN films grown on sapphire substrates have the best crystalline quality and optical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the substrate is the dominant factor determining the properties of the GaN film.
it is possible to grow high quality films of GaN on GaN substrates, which are free from defects and have good luminescence characteristics.
the substrate type has a profound effect on the structural and optical characteristics of the epitaxial film.
